summary: A passage from Book 11, part 37 of a novel (Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm style, set in Riverboro) in which Rebecca Randall, on the day of a school event, finds her lunch left by her aunts and decides to wear the pink gingham dress her aunt Jane had just finished, without asking permission. She dresses up, admires herself in the parlor mirror, and hurries to school, where Emma Jane Perkins admires her appearance. Emma Jane plans to wear her mother's garnet ring for the flag-pointing part of the program, and Rebecca worries about whether her aunts would approve.
one_line: Rebecca Randall secretly wears her new pink gingham dress to school in Riverboro while her aunts are away.
key_facts: Rebecca Randall finds a note from aunt Jane saying that the aunts had gone to Moderation with Mrs. Robinson in her carryall.
The pink gingham dress was finished by aunt Jane's kind hands.
Rebecca decides to wear the pink gingham dress without asking, reasoning that 'they're not here to ask'.
Rebecca fastens all but the three middle buttons of the dress, which she reserves for Emma Jane.
Rebecca's pink sunshade is an exact match for the pink gingham dress, and the girls had never seen it.
Rebecca plans to wrap the sunshade in paper, show it at school, and carry it coming home.
Rebecca pulls a pink rose from a bush at the gate before running to school.
It was twenty minutes to one when Rebecca left, and she was afraid she would be late.
Rebecca finds the key to the side door under the step, as everybody in Riverboro did.
Emma Jane says Rebecca is 'handsome as a picture' and 'different somehow'.
Emma Jane plans to wear her mother's garnet ring so it would flash in the sun when she points to the flag.
Emma Jane's mother scrubbed the garnet ring in soap and water.
Emma Jane asks how Rebecca's aunt Mirandy allowed her to put on the new dress, and Rebecca answers that both aunts were away.
